ety.text: From Latin exquīsītus (“to be outsought”), perfect passive participle of exquīrō (“to outseek”).

senses.d: Especially or extraordinarily fine or pleasing; exceptional.
ex: They sell good coffee and pastries, but their chocolate is exquisite.
Sourav Ganguly scored an exquisite century in his debut Test match.

senses.d: Of special beauty or rare excellence.
Exceeding; extreme; keen, in a bad or a good sense.
Of delicate perception or close and accurate discrimination; not easy to satisfy; exact; fastidious.
ex: his books of Oriental languages, wherein he was exquisite
